section_summary: This section documents major narcotics-smuggling cases in Dairen, especially the importation of benzoylmorphine and heroin under loopholes and allegedly falsified provisions of Kwantung Government Order No. 54. It follows the defendants’ prosecution and eventual acquittal, reports police raids on illicit morphine operations, and supplies regulatory texts and information about the Kwantung opium monopoly. The later papers concern the arrest and trial of American citizen George I. Tribe and an international group suspected of financing and distributing narcotics through Dairen, Harbin, and northern China.

subfiles.title: Narcotic Traffic Notes and Manchuria Daily News enclosure
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Tokyo, with copies to the Department of State and other posts
subfiles.about: Reports a large, organized scheme for importing benzoylmorphine and heroin into Dairen under a transitional clause in Kwantung narcotics regulations.
subfiles.summary: The closing page of Langdon’s despatch is followed by a Manchuria Daily News article describing three Japanese smuggling groups. The groups allegedly falsified contracts, shipment dates, and certificates to make new German and Swiss purchases appear to predate the 1927 regulations. Police arrested most suspects and seized a large stock consigned to Matsuuchi, although Tsunemitsu and Hiramatsu remained at large.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note for Despatch No. 125
subfiles.from: Department of State Index Bureau
subfiles.about: Indexes a Dairen report about fourteen Japanese suspects turned over for prosecution under the Kwantung narcotics regulations.
subfiles.summary: The sheet cross-references Despatch No. 125 to another narcotics file. It states that Dairen police transferred fourteen Japanese suspects to the public procurator on May 28, 1930, and that they were indicted after a preliminary hearing.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 124 on “benzoline”
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a Dairen report concerning a narcotic first called benzoin and later described as benzoline or possibly benzoylmorphine.
subfiles.summary: The State Department transmits Langdon’s September 13 despatch for the Bureau of Narcotics. It notes that Kwantung Order No. 54 covered drugs designated by the governor as having effects similar to morphine or cocaine. Because Japanese scientific terminology was difficult to translate, the Department suggests that the substance may have been benzoylmorphine.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 137 with Japan Chronicle clippings on the Dairen drug trial
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits three newspaper reports on hearings in the Dairen benzoylmorphine and heroin prosecution.
subfiles.summary: The clippings describe charges against three groups accused of importing drugs worth more than two million yen through fraudulent claims that the shipments were already in transit. Defense counsel challenged whether benzoylmorphine was legally prohibited, because the relevant language appeared only in an erratum to the ordinance. Shirakawa described his negotiations with Governor Kinoshita, Police Director Kubo, and sanitation official Kawai, while an expert testified that benzoylmorphine and heroin were salts of morphine derivatives. Later argument concerned witnesses, the original ordinance draft, and Kawai’s acceptance of a platinum watch.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 137 to the Treasury
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the Tokyo Embassy’s despatch and clippings about prosecutions for benzoylmorphine and heroin trafficking in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends Despatch No. 137 and its enclosures to the Commissioner of Narcotics. The material concerns persons prosecuted for complicity in illicit benzoylmorphine and heroin traffic.

subfiles.title: Transmittal and clipping on the Kwantung opium monopoly
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits an April 24 Japan Chronicle clipping concerning the government opium monopoly in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The covering letter forwards a photostat for the Commissioner of Narcotics. The surviving clipping page supplies only the headline “An Opium Monopoly: The Profits of Suppression.”

subfiles.title: Transmittal and Japan Weekly Chronicle clipping on narcotics seizures
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards reports of a morphine seizure in Dairen and the prosecution of an Osaka narcotics ring.
subfiles.summary: The clipping describes a police raid on a Dairen medicine-company branch, where morphine and Japanese employees were seized, and reports another suspected illicit factory. A second article concerns Asada Mantaro, Kitada Koji, and Asai Sentaro, accused at Osaka of smuggling morphine and cocaine worth about three million yen. The page also contains unrelated newspaper columns on cotton, railway economies, an estate suit, and murders.

subfiles.title: Instruction to report on the Dairen morphine cases
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Directs the consul to report fully on recent morphine seizures and factories in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Castle cites the June 4 Japan Weekly Chronicle report of a large May 18 seizure at the Medicine Manufacturing Company in Mikasa-machi. Langdon is asked to investigate both that case and another illicit factory and to transmit relevant Manchuria Daily News articles.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 198: Benzoylin Smuggling Case, Dairen
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reviews the benzoylmorphine and heroin importations and reports allegations that officials altered the text of Kwantung Order No. 54.
subfiles.summary: Langdon explains the original ordinance, its published errata, and the quantities imported by Komatsu, Shirakawa, and Matsuuchi through fraudulent contracts and certificates. He reports that 5,550 kilograms were unlawfully imported and largely sold while Governors Kodama and Kinoshita were in office. At trial the defendants argued that an erratum could not lawfully add salts of derivatives to the prohibited list. Chikamori’s testimony that Kawai had the original text altered led to forgery proceedings against both officials and threatened to collapse the narcotics prosecution.

subfiles.title: Confidential Despatch No. 199: Notes on Narcotic Traffic
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports an Indian police inquiry into a possible Port Arthur narcotics factory, four recent Dairen cases, and questions about the Kwantung opium monopoly.
subfiles.summary: Deputy Inspector General J. Slattery sought the source of Fuji Tsuru cocaine and investigated claims that a protected factory operated at Port Arthur. Langdon then catalogs four police cases involving imported cocaine or ecgonine and illicit morphine production at Dairen factories. He suspects the sudden raids may have been prompted by Slattery’s visit and considers seeking official case information under the American-Japanese exchange arrangement. The concluding material discusses proposals to bring confiscated morphine into the government monopoly system.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of Despatch No. 199
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Langdon’s confidential report on illicit narcotics and the Kwantung Government opium monopoly.
subfiles.summary: The State Department encloses Despatch No. 199 for the Acting Commissioner of Narcotics. It identifies both illicit narcotics traffic and the operations of the Kwantung opium monopoly as subjects of the report.

subfiles.title: Circular instruction and questionnaire package on narcotics laws
subfiles.doc_type: circular instruction with questionnaire and annexes
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: American diplomatic officers and certain American consular officers
subfiles.about: Requests authoritative information on narcotics laws throughout foreign countries, colonies, and dependencies for use by the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: The package lists the principal Kwantung opium and narcotics enactments and includes part of the erratum to the 1927 regulation. The circular explains that accurate legal information is needed to enforce United States import and export laws and to support international narcotics control. Its annex identifies consular offices and the territories for which each is to obtain material, ranging from Gibraltar and India to Kwantung, Korea, Taiwan, Indonesia, and the Free City of Danzig.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 215 and enclosure: Acquittals in the benzoylin case
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the acquittal of the benzoylmorphine defendants because the ordinance’s corrective errata lacked legal force.
subfiles.summary: The Dairen District Court acquitted the narcotics defendants on July 24, holding that the published erratum could not expand Order No. 54 to cover salts of derivatives. Shirakawa alone was fined 300 yen for bribing a Kwantung official. Langdon notes public surprise given the evidence of fraud, perjury, and forgery, and reports that the procurator appealed to the Supreme Court at Port Arthur. The enclosed article reproduces Chief Judge Morimoto’s defense of judicial independence.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 214: Narcotic Traffic, Dairen
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Answers the Department’s request for information about recent narcotics seizures in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Langdon states that Despatch No. 199 already fully reported the cases and identifies the Medicine Manufacturing Company raid as case four. He declines to send numerous confusing press articles unless specifically requested. The Kwantung Government has been informally asked to supply useful information arising from the judicial proceedings.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Dairen narcotics despatches Nos. 198, 214, and 215
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards confidential Dairen reports concerning illicit manufacture and German and Swiss drug imports.
subfiles.summary: The Department identifies the factory case reported in the Japan Weekly Chronicle as case four in Despatch No. 199. It also sends Despatches Nos. 198 and 215 on the prosecution of Japanese subjects for importing narcotics from Germany and Switzerland.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 219: Official reply on four narcotics cases
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Relays the Kwantung Government’s response to Langdon’s inquiry about four recently reported Dairen narcotics cases.
subfiles.summary: The authorities deny that Ihara transshipped cocaine from Germany through Dairen or that Dairen police made the reported seizure in case one. They state that no local investigation or judgment occurred in that matter. They confirm that the press accounts of cases two through four were substantially accurate.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 219
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Langdon’s report on illicit narcotics traffic in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The letter sends a copy of Despatch No. 219 to the Commissioner of Narcotics. It links the report to the Department’s earlier August 24 correspondence.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 235 and translation of Kwantung Government Order No. 54
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Supplies an amended translation of the principal Kwantung regulation governing narcotics.
subfiles.summary: Langdon identifies Order No. 54 and three opium enactments as the complete body of Kwantung narcotics legislation. The translation defines narcotics, requires gubernatorial authorization for manufacture, import, and export, regulates possession and recordkeeping, and states applicable penalties. It also treats landing or transshipment as import or export and makes employers or corporate representatives responsible for certain violations.

subfiles.title: Fragment on cocaine consumption in Kwantung
subfiles.about: Calculates per-capita cocaine consumption in the Kwantung Leased Territory and evaluates the importance of a four-kilogram importation.
subfiles.summary: The fragment states that the 1930 cocaine allowance or consumption was ten kilograms for a population of 1.2 million. It calculates consumption at 8.53 kilograms per million inhabitants and concludes that a single four-kilogram import would be highly material for Dairen.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 235 and Order No. 54
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Langdon’s despatch and the translated Kwantung narcotics regulation to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends Despatch No. 235 of November 2 and its enclosure, Order No. 54 of September 28, 1927. The documents concern narcotics control in the Kwantung Leased Territory.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the arrest of George I. Tribe
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the arrest of an American citizen with Japanese, Russian, and French suspects in a narcotics and arms case.
subfiles.summary: George I. Tribe was arrested on November 21 with several foreign and Japanese suspects, reportedly for narcotics trafficking and arms smuggling into China. Dairen police confirmed his detention but withheld the formal charges during the preliminary investigation. Langdon notes that the authorities’ reticence departed from their usual practice and that a conspiracy charge could raise legal questions about punishing an American for conduct affecting China.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting a full report on the Tribe case
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Orders a full report and rapid notice of any United States connections in the Tribe narcotics case.
subfiles.summary: Stimson refers to the consul’s December 1 despatch to the Embassy. He requests a full mailed report and immediate telegraphic notice of narcotics developments, especially any possible connection with the United States.

subfiles.title: Letter to Treasury concerning Tribe and six arrested foreigners
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Provides the Treasury with a newspaper clipping and preliminary biographical information about George I. Tribe.
subfiles.summary: The letter reports that Tribe, a naturalized American of Russian birth, was among foreigners arrested at Dairen on suspected narcotics and arms charges. It notes that the consul has been ordered to report fully and to examine possible American connections. Tribe’s stated San Francisco residence, his acquaintance N. Homsky, a photograph, and a personal description are supplied to the Treasury.

subfiles.title: Instruction and New York Times clipping on Dairen arrests
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests a complete investigation of reports that foreigners were arrested for narcotics trafficking from a Dairen base.
subfiles.summary: The Department states that Dairen may have served as a base for smuggling narcotics to the United States as well as distributing them in Manchuria. The enclosed New York Times item reports arrests for separate arms and narcotics conspiracies, including six foreigners tied to a large European drug organization. It claims that narcotics worth more than 1.5 million yen were imported at Dairen and distributed across Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Confidential despatch on George I. Tribe’s arrest and background
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports confidential Kwantung information about Tribe’s alleged offense, detention, legal exposure, and personal history.
subfiles.summary: Langdon discusses Tribe’s treatment in detention and estimates that Order No. 54 exposed him to no more than one year’s imprisonment or a 200-yen fine. He records Tribe’s birth at Pinsk, naturalization in San Francisco, residence in Dairen, and partnership with M. Triguboff in the Manchuria Import Company. Although Tribe had a prior customs dispute, Langdon describes him as socially respectable and probably a tool of his brother and Henri Bacri Cohen rather than a principal trafficker.

subfiles.title: Despatch on indictments in the Tribe-Cohen-Takushima case
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports that Tribe and most other suspects were formally indicted for violating Kwantung narcotics regulations.
subfiles.summary: Langdon says the accused, with one or two exceptions, have been indicted and will be tried in the Dairen District Court. Available information remains scant pending trial, but Henri Bacri Cohen and R. Takushima are described as leading figures; Tribe and Soviet Russian Jacob D. Lelgitsky are among those involved. Langdon attributes discovery of the operation to information his office furnished in September and presents the case as evidence of useful American-Japanese cooperation.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmittal of the December 21 and 22 Tribe despatches
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards two confidential consular reports on the arrest of Tribe and other suspected narcotics traffickers.
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends copies of Langdon’s December 21 and 22 despatches to the Commissioner of Narcotics. It also refers to earlier information about Henri Bacri Cohen and R. Takushima. The Commissioner is asked to consult the State Department before raising the case directly with Japanese authorities under the informal information-exchange arrangement.

subfiles.title: Strictly confidential Despatch No. 224 and memorandum on Bacri and Takushima
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; memorandum delivered to the Kwantung Government
subfiles.about: Provides financial intelligence alleging that Henri Bacri Cohen and R. Takushima were arranging narcotics purchases through Paris and Hamburg.
subfiles.summary: Langdon states that the Dairen branch of the National City Bank of New York supplied the information, which he passed to the governor’s representative. The memorandum says Bacri arranged large remittances to Louis Lyon in Paris under the guise of silk imports and dealt extensively with Takushima. Takushima’s bicycle-importing firm allegedly remitted substantial sums to a Hamburg concern suspected of brokering narcotics, including an expense account for travel to Switzerland.

subfiles.title: Confidential Despatch No. 244: Opening of Tribe’s trial
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the opening of George Tribe’s trial and his denial of any connection to narcotics smuggling into the United States.
subfiles.summary: Langdon says Tribe’s trial opened on February 2 and recounts a private interview conducted while Tribe was on bond. Tribe admitted acting for fees as an intermediary in three local purchases made for Dairen and Harbin operators, with delivery to smugglers serving the interior. He believed the Bacri-Takushima transactions and Dairen narcotics traffic were directed toward the Manchurian hinterland and northern China, not the United States, while acknowledging that his knowledge was limited.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Despatch No. 244
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Langdon’s report on Tribe’s pending narcotics trial to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends a copy of Despatch No. 244, dated February 2. It notes that Tribe was then on trial for participating in illicit narcotics traffic.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment and San Francisco agent’s report
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Stuart J. Fuller
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Tribe despatch and forwards a narcotics agent’s San Francisco report.
subfiles.summary: The Treasury acknowledges receipt of the State Department’s March 7 communication and Langdon’s February 2 despatch. It encloses, for State’s information, a March 4 report from a narcotics agent at San Francisco concerning Tribe’s alleged complicity.
